newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Telinfo starts year with a bang.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Telinfo starts year with a bang.

text.p: Belgian data communications company Telinfo NV said on Friday it signed several lucrative contracts around the New Year which would help it maintain future earnings growth.
"Just before or after New Year, we have been awarded a number of important agreements," Telinfo chairman John Cordier told a news conference.
"And January looks like it is going to be a top month, it exceeded all expectations," Cordier said.
He said Telecom Italia awarded it a contract worth 130 million Belgian francs for the supply of switchgear.
Telinfo also obtained a contract worth 80 to 85 million francs from a Polish telecoms company for high-speed modems which allow analogue lines to be digitalised.
"This is a new product which we brought onto the market at the end of 1996...There is a lot of interest for the product which we developed ourselves," Cordier said.
He added that Telinfo was among the world elite for digitalisation, together with a U.S. and European company which he declined to name.
He said he expected Telinfo's group pre-tax profit to rise 20 percent in 1997 and turnover to rise 17 percent.
Telinfo also won a deal with leading Belgian bank Generale Bank worth 80 million francs.

In addition, Telinfo also won a contract late last year from Belgian telecommunications start-up Telenet Operaties NV, which aims to convert Flanders' extensive cable television network to provide multimedia and voice telephone services from late 1997.
Telindus Nortel, a joint venture between Telinfo and Canada's Northern Telecom, will supply Telenet's digital telephone exchanges.
The final contract was signed earlier this week, Cordier said.
He said that one of the backbones of future growth for Telinfo would be the digitalisation of analogue equipment.
In Belgium alone, there were 80,000 analogue circuits which had to be digitalised, he said.
An expected surge in use of GSM mobile phones and the Internet and Intranets in the years ahead would also bolster Telinfo's business, he said.
